entries.sense_en: until this time; up to now

synonyms.nuance: The everyday way to say it; hitherto is formal or old-fashioned.
synonyms.example: Until now, she had worn them.

synonyms.nuance: Neutral and common; simply means 'before', without the sense of 'up to this point'.
synonyms.example: She had previously lived in Paris.

synonyms.nuance: Even more formal; mostly found in legal documents today.

entries.sense_en: moved in a hurried, clumsy way, dragging her feet

synonyms.nuance: Walking slowly without lifting the feet; tired or old, not hurried.
synonyms.example: He shuffled to the door in his slippers.

synonyms.nuance: Moving fast and awkwardly, often using hands too; more urgent.
synonyms.example: She scrambled out of the way.

synonyms.nuance: Quick short steps, like a small animal hurrying away.

entries.tip_ko: 오늘날 scuffle은 주로 '몸싸움, 드잡이'라는 뜻으로 쓰입니다.

entries.sense_en: taken and held firmly; grabbed

synonyms.nuance: Everyday and quick; a sudden, rough taking.
synonyms.example: He grabbed the slipper and ran.

synonyms.nuance: Stronger and more forceful; also used for police or armies taking things.
Modern form; also means to obtain or to contact someone.
synonyms.example: I couldn't get hold of her.

entries.sense_en: a poor, dirty, often naughty child who plays in the streets

synonyms.nuance: A spoiled, badly behaved child; about behavior, not poverty.
Stresses ragged, dirty clothes; old-fashioned and a little affectionate.
synonyms.example: a little ragamuffin in torn shoes

synonyms.nuance: A playfully naughty person; usually said with fondness.

entries.sense_en: very well; excellently

synonyms.nuance: Modern, neutral; stresses that nothing is lacking.
Also a little old-fashioned but still heard; adds admiration.
Milder and casual; good enough, pleasant.

entries.sense_en: whole and long (stressing how long the day felt)

synonyms.nuance: Plain and neutral; livelong adds a feeling that the time dragged.
Slightly more formal than whole; no emotional color.
The natural modern phrase with the same weary feeling.

entries.sense_en: an old British coin worth a quarter of a penny; a tiny amount of money
entries.sense_ko: 파딩(옛 영국의 아주 작은 동전), 한 푼

synonyms.nuance: A real modern coin; "not a penny" is today's way to say no money at all.
American equivalent in idioms: "not a cent".
American ten-cent coin; used in "not worth a dime".

entries.modern: "not a single farthing" → "not a single penny"

entries.sense_en: moved slowly and quietly, close to the ground or walls

synonyms.nuance: Moving on hands and knees, or extremely slowly like traffic.
synonyms.example: The baby crawled across the floor.

synonyms.nuance: Moving quietly in order not to be seen; suggests a secret purpose.
synonyms.example: He sneaked out of the house.

synonyms.nuance: Walking on the toes to make no noise.

entries.tip_ko: creep - crept - crept 불규칙 변화에 주의하세요.

entries.sense_en: a perfect example of a quality or feeling

synonyms.nuance: Usually means looking exactly like a person ("the image of her mother").
synonyms.example: He's the image of his father.

synonyms.nuance: More formal; a person who fully represents an idea.
Formal; the most typical example of a type.

entries.modern: "the very picture of health/misery" is still used

entries.sense_en: shining with a soft, steady light

synonyms.nuance: Many tiny flashing points of light, like jewels or tinsel.
Warm, steady light without flame, like embers or a lamp.
Faint, weak, unsteady light.
synonyms.example: a glimmer of light in the distance

entries.sense_en: bent down low and made her body small (from cold and fear)

synonyms.nuance: Neutral; bending the knees low, for any reason, not only fear.
Pulling the body in tightly, often for warmth, or crowding together.
Pulling back suddenly in fear or embarrassment; a quick movement.

entries.sense_en: dare to do something risky or unpleasant

synonyms.nuance: The common word; focuses on courage rather than on going somewhere.
Stresses possible loss or danger as the result.
synonyms.example: I won't risk losing my job.

synonyms.nuance: Facing something hard directly, e.g. weather or danger.

entries.sense_en: hard hits with the hand or a weapon

synonyms.nuance: A hit specifically with a closed fist.
A hit with an open hand, often on the face.
A series of hits, a whole attack; "get a beating" is the modern phrase.
synonyms.example: He got a beating from his father.

entries.sense_en: made unable to feel anything because of cold

synonyms.nuance: Very cold, often exaggerated in daily speech ("my hands are frozen").
Hard to move, not necessarily without feeling.
Informal: a body part with no feeling, often from pressure.

entries.sense_en: give or provide

synonyms.nuance: Neutral, very common; afford in this sense is formal or literary.
Suggests something made available, which may be accepted or not.
synonyms.example: The window offers a fine view.

synonyms.nuance: The simplest everyday word.

entries.tip_ko: '(돈이) 여유가 있다'가 아니라 '주다, 제공하다'라는 격식 있는 뜻입니다.

entries.sense_en: burned brightly and strongly with a big flame

synonyms.nuance: A sudden, short burst of flame.
Burning unsteadily, going weak and strong.
Steady light and heat without large flames.

entries.sense_en: (of metal) polished until it shines

synonyms.nuance: Everyday word; for any surface, including wood and shoes.
Simply describes shine, not the rubbing that made it.
Shining brightly, often very clean; stresses the light.

entries.sense_en: clear, so that you can see through it

synonyms.nuance: Informal; common for clothes and thin fabrics.
Lets light through, but you cannot see shapes clearly.
Plain everyday word for glass, water or plastic.

entries.sense_en: look at or see (something remarkable)

synonyms.nuance: Neutral everyday word; behold is literary and solemn.
Looking at something that moves or changes, for some time.
Looking for a long time, often in wonder or love.

entries.sense_en: walked unsteadily, swaying from side to side

synonyms.nuance: Walking unsteadily because of weakness, injury or drink; the closest synonym.
synonyms.example: He staggered under the heavy load.

synonyms.nuance: Small unsteady steps, as if about to fall; often old people or babies.
Moving gently from side to side, not necessarily while walking.
synonyms.example: The trees swayed in the wind.

entries.sense_en: a long line left behind by something moving

synonyms.nuance: A thin line of color or light, often quick and sharp.
The end part trailing behind, as of a comet or kite.
Marks on the ground left by feet or wheels.

entries.sense_en: goes up, rises (here, to heaven)

synonyms.nuance: Everyday word for moving up; ascend is formal or solemn.
Going up with effort, often using hands and feet.
Flying up high quickly and freely, like a bird.
synonyms.example: The eagle soared into the sky.

entries.sense_en: a soft, shining light

synonyms.nuance: Soft shine on a surface such as hair or silk.
Warm, steady light coming from inside something.
Very strong, bright light; much more intense.

entries.modern: in the lustre → in the light / glow (US spelling: luster)

entries.sense_en: shining with light, and looking very happy and beautiful

synonyms.nuance: Plain word for light or cheerful; less emotional and poetic.
Smiling widely with happiness; about the face.
Softer light; also healthy-looking skin or warm praise.

entries.sense_en: disappeared suddenly and completely

synonyms.nuance: Neutral, everyday; can be sudden or gradual.
synonyms.example: The sun disappeared behind a cloud.

synonyms.nuance: Disappearing slowly and gradually, becoming weaker.
Gradually disappearing, like snow or a crowd.

entries.sense_en: in the past; before this time

synonyms.nuance: Very close; slightly more common in news and business.
Simple and a little storylike: at some time in the past.
Refers to a nearer past, often the same day or period.

entries.tip_ko: formally(격식을 갖춰)와 발음이 비슷하니 철자에 주의하세요.

entries.sense_en: completely stiff and rigid (here, because she had died of cold)

synonyms.nuance: Unable to bend; neutral, also used for rules and people.
Modern phrase: completely frozen, or informally just very cold.
Alone today it usually means bare or harsh, as in "a stark contrast".

entries.sense_en: a slight idea or feeling that something is true

synonyms.nuance: The plain word: "no one had the slightest idea" is today's usual phrase.
Informal; a feeling based on intuition, not facts.
synonyms.example: I have a hunch he'll come.

synonyms.nuance: A very slight hint of knowledge; often negative ("not an inkling").
synonyms.example: She had no inkling of the plan.

entries.sense_en: great beauty and brightness that fills you with wonder

synonyms.nuance: Stresses grand size and impressive richness.
Impressive and noble greatness, often of places or events.
Great beauty with a sense of honor or heavenly light.
